claim: 重建即同内容：两次独立构建在去掉两处时间戳后逐字段一致，图为逐字节一致。

method.isolation: each run re-logs in and re-fetches GET /api/v1/tensor/reports/13494, then builds into its own fresh temp directory; the second run does not read the first
method.hash_gate: both runs must reproduce contract source_hash sha256:ad61f9e0bc3dbe8c8f4ae40ce90056f06c98477c9a33302193f8297756783abe (else build() aborts)

normalised_fields.kf_result.outputs.asset_manifest.json.pa: rewritten to docs/kf/wp-13494-01/asset_manifest.json: each determinism run builds into its own temp directory by design; the committed run's value is asserted separately by verification.json::manifest_hash_matches_envelope and published_check.json

method.figure_comparison: PNG bytes compared directly (no canonicalisation, no metadata stripping)

expected_differences.reason: raw bytes carry each run's build clock (generated_at) and therefore also the envelope's digest of them; both are listed in method.excluded_volatile_fields and compared after removal

verdict: deterministic: identical canonical content and byte-identical figure
limitations: Raw output bytes are deliberately NOT identical: every run records its own build clock (asset_manifest.generated_at, kf_result.provenance.emitted_at). Those two fields are named above and removed before hashing; no other field may drift.
Determinism is asserted for one machine/toolchain (see environment); cross-platform byte equality of matplotlib-rendered PNG is out of scope.
The scan itself has no randomness (no sampling, no dict-order dependence): asset order is document order, so identical content also means identical asset_id -> span mapping.
